ev.q: To examine the role of sexual transmission, a matched case-control study and viral analysis were conducted.
Sexual transmission was found to be the most likely mode of transmission of HCV
Of the 74 patients, 65 (91%) had a previous negative HCV-antibody test result
case-patients were significantly more likely than controls to report receptive anal intercourse
receptive anal intercourse with no condom and with ejaculation of the partner (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 23.00)
a matched case-control study was conducted beginning in July 2007.
Mount Sinai evaluated 74 HIV-infected MSM who reported no injection-drug use

methods_quotes.q: a conditional logistic regression of each variable (i.e., sexual practice or drug use behavior) was performed.
Those variables that had a p value of ≤0.20 in the univariable analysis
were entered into a model and analyzed using multivariable conditional logistic regression (i.e., forward, backward, and stepwise)
the data were analyzed further using exact conditional logistic regression
A maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree was then created
